\subsection{Sampled Parcel-Label Trajectory}\label{sec:label_trajectory}
The separate diagnostic run \texttt{manuscript42\_seed42\_8cbb8ee} uses the manuscript coupled
configuration ($N=40$, six computational parcels per species, seed 42,
             \texttt{MersenneTwister}) and records 101 labelled states from MCS 0 through 100.
Its initial registry and lattice both contain 42 parcels, with six for each of seven species.
The fixed interior contains 50,200 sites, including initially empty sites.
At one-MCS sampling, the parcel-ID sequence contains 12,682 adjacent-frame label transitions and 2,933 completed return episodes; the species sequence contains 10,453 transitions and 2,671 returns.
A return is an observed departure from the MCS-0 reference label followed by a later arrival at that label.
Unchanged-at-every-saved-frame parcel identity holds at 44,990/50,200 interior sites (89.62\%); this includes empty-site identity.
Initial-species and initial-parcel strata, their denominators and persistence curves are retained in the run data.
Binary species-indicator means report sampled occupancy; integer label codes are never averaged.

The ordered accepted-copy record contains 14,281 events and replays the complete label-state hash at every MCS.
It records 3,510 parcel-ID and 3,213 species return episodes at event resolution.
These event counts and the sampled counts have different temporal resolution; only the event record resolves ordering within a sweep.
The instrumented and uninstrumented complete states and RNG continuation agree exactly; one-MCS and 100-MCS windows also agree.
The original coupled runner agrees at MCS 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100. A tenfold uptake-parameter perturbation leaves the labelled trajectory unchanged.
The radiodialysis basis acknowledgement is restricted to this label diagnostic: mobile and sorbed quantities remain blocked and are neither analysed nor displayed.
This is one deterministic computational trajectory, without an uncertainty estimate or biological-effect inference.
